edges.description: Developmental delay is the usual presenting manifestation.
Intellectual disability of mild to severe degree is a defining feature.
Speech and language are disproportionately affected.
Hypotonia is a frequent neurological manifestation.
Gait abnormality ranges from tip-toe to unsteady walking.
Stereotypies and chorea occur in a minority.
Autism spectrum disorder is a defining behavioral feature.
Epilepsy affects a minority of individuals.
A recognizable but non-specific facial gestalt accompanies the neurologic phenotype.
Congenital heart defects occur in a minority of individuals.
Thoracic scoliosis is among the reported skeletal anomalies.
Difficulty with swallowing and chewing was reported by families and physicians.
Inguinal hernia was reported and often required early repair.
Hypospadias was reported and often required early repair.
Bilateral moyamoya angiopathy has been reported in an individual with a de novo SETD5 frameshift variant, but the association is not yet validated.

nodes.description: SETD5 governs RNA polymerase II dynamics through its interaction with the HDAC3 and PAF1 complexes and through the H3K36me3 mark it places on gene bodies. evidence.reference_title: Expansion and further delineation of the SETD5 phenotype leading to global developmental delay, variable dysmorphic features, and reduced penetrance.
evidence.snippet: The majority of patients in this cohort and previously reported have developmental delay, behavioral/psychiatric issues, and variable hand and skeletal abnormalities.

nodes.description: Epilepsy affects a minority of individuals, with heterogeneous seizure types including epileptic spasms and focal motor and non-motor seizures. Notably, none of the seven individuals in the original gene-discovery cohort had seizures, whereas 14% of the later multicenter cohort did - the seizure phenotype emerged only as the cohort broadened.

evidence.reference_title: Neurological and psychiatric phenotype of a multicenter cohort of patients with SETD5-related neurodevelopmental disorder.
evidence.snippet: Epilepsy was present in about 14 % of patients, including different types of seizures as epileptic spasms, focal motor, and non-motor seizures.

evidence.reference_title: De novo loss-of-function mutations in SETD5, encoding a methyltransferase in a 3p25 microdeletion syndrome critical region, cause intellectual disability.
evidence.snippet: Growth parameters were within the normal range in all children, none had micro- cephaly or seizures

evidence.reference_title: A Novel Epilepsy Phenotype in a Young Girl With a Pathogenic SETD5 Gene Variant.
evidence.snippet: Our findings confirm that epilepsy may arise after SETD5 variants, with subtle clinical manifestations that may overlap with behavioral phenomena in children who also exhibit cognitive and behavioral comorbidities.
